content.title: About
content.content: Meringues are light, airy desserts made from whipped egg whites and sugar. Sometimes starch, lemon juice, or flavorings are added. After baking they become crisp on the outside and tender inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Meringues originated in France in the 17th century and quickly spread across Europe.
The name “meringue” is linked to Swiss confectioner Joseph Meringue, who is said to have created them in 1692.
There are several types: French (whipped whites and sugar only), Swiss (sugar melted with whites), and Italian (hot sugar syrup poured into whipped whites).
Meringues are often used as the base for Pavlova and Baked Alaska desserts.
When properly baked, meringues can be stored for several weeks in a dry place.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Meringues contain virtually no fat, making them a light dessert when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Egg whites provide a modest amount of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Traditional meringues are naturally gluten‑free, suitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B2
items.content: Egg whites contain riboflavin (vitamin B2), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calorie‑friendly with fruit toppings
items.content: Serving meringues with berries or fruit sauce adds vitamins and fiber without greatly increasing calories.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Meringues contain egg whites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The large amount of sugar makes meringues calorie‑dense and can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: If made from raw eggs without sufficient heat treatment, there is a risk of salmonella.

items.title: Fragility
items.content: Meringues crumble easily, posing a choking hazard for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Meringues can be enjoyed on their own, used as cake decorations, served with berry sauce, ice cream, or fresh fruit. They can also be crushed and folded into mousses or creams for a light texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store finished meringues in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Properly stored they stay crisp for 2–3 weeks. If they become soft, they can be re‑dried in a low‑temperature oven.
